q1: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
q2: SELECT DISTINCT A.CUSTOMER_ID AS CUSTOMER_ID FROM (SELECT CUSTOMER_ID, COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) AS NUM_PRODUCTS FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY CUSTOMER_ID)A JOIN (SELECT COUNT(PRODUCT_KEY) AS NUM_PRODUCTS FROM PRODUCT)B ON(A.NUM_PRODUCTS = B.NUM_PRODUCTS) WHERE A.CUSTOMER_ID IS NOT NULL
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT A.CUSTOMER_ID AS CUSTOMER_ID FROM (SELECT CUSTOMER_ID, COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) AS NUM_PRODUCTS FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY CUSTOMER_ID)A JOIN (SELECT COUNT(PRODUCT_KEY) AS NUM_PRODUCTS FROM PRODUCT)B ON(A.NUM_PRODUCTS = B.NUM_PRODUCTS) WHERE A.CUSTOMER_ID IS NOT NULL
counterexample: INSERT INTO PRODUCT (PRODUCT_KEY) VALUES (1), (2), (3); INSERT INTO CUSTOMER (CUSTOMER_ID, PRODUCT_KEY) VALUES (1, 1), (1, 2), (1, 3);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent. Q1 selects customer IDs where the count of distinct product keys is equal to the total count of distinct product keys in the product table. Q2 selects customer IDs where the count of distinct product keys is equal to the total count of product keys in the product table, which is incorrect as it should be the count of distinct product keys.
counterexample_dsp: A customer who has purchased all products in the product table.
